title: Microexemplar Tinkerbox: vignette seeds & negative probes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal lab for micro-exemplar experiments: compact few-shot vignettes + antipode/negative probes to expose brittle behaviors and provide robust example pairs for the prompt library. This is intentionally messy — notes-to-self, candidate shot-sets, and quick eval checks.

High-level hypotheses:
- Short, strongly-contrasted exemplars (3–4 tokens of difference) reduce hallucination on slot-filling tasks more than semantically distant negatives.
- ‘Soft negatives’ (plausible-but-wrong answers) are more effective at steering models away from confident mistakes than obvious absurd negatives.
- Mixing one canonical exemplar with 2-3 adversarial exemplars yields a better tradeoff between precision and diversity than a homogeneous set.

Experiment matrix (priority order):
1) Intent-to-slot tasks (address/phone/email extraction) — compare canonical + soft-negative vs canonical + absurd-negative.
2) Preference inversion probes — few-shot pairs that show claim then correction. Test transfer to unseen claim formats.
3) Tone anchoring — 1 warm example, 1 terse example, then adversarial example to see tone stability.
4) Token-budget ablations — move exemplar length from 16 tokens total to 64 tokens. Measure top-1 answer stability.

Quick scoring rubric (manual for now):
- Correctness: exact-match or normalized-match (lower, strip punctuation)
- Overconfidence: model asserts but includes wrong facts — penalize strongly
- Compliance: avoided unsafe/forbidden completion when instruction demands refusal

Candidate micro-exemplar sets (format: instruction + fewshots)
A. Slot extraction (canonical + soft negative)
Instruction: Extract the customer name and order number from the message.
Example 1 (good):
Message: "Hi — this is Nora Jenkins. Order # 8421 arrived damaged."
Answer: "name: Nora Jenkins; order: 8421"
Example 2 (soft negative):
Message: "I think my order was placed by Nora J. but the name shows N. Jenkins — order 8421- A?"
Answer: "name: Nora Jenkins; order: 8421"

B. Slot extraction (canonical + absurd negative)
Example 1 (good): same as above
Example 2 (absurd negative):
Message: "The binary code 110101 indicates the courier. Call 867-5309 for pizza."
Answer: "name: Nora Jenkins; order: 8421"  <-- expected, but this negative is obviously unrelated

C. Preference inversion (correction microshots)
Instruction: Decide which statement is true. If both are false, say 'neither'.
Example 1: "A says the product ships in 2 days. B says it ships in 2 weeks." Answer: "A is true; B is false"
Example 2 (correction): "A says product shipped in 2 days; later: Actually A confused shipping & processing; product shipped in 2 weeks." Answer: "B is true; correct the record to 2 weeks"

D. Tone anchoring (warm vs terse)
Instruction: Reply to user with the requested update in the specified tone.
Example 1 (warm): "Tone: warm
User: Please confirm my billing address."
Answer: "Hi! Happy to help — I’ve confirmed your billing address as 123 Elm St. Anything else I can check for you?"
Example 2 (terse): "Tone: terse
User: Please confirm my billing address."
Answer: "Billing address: 123 Elm St."
Example 3 (adversarial close): "Tone: terse
User: Please confirm my billing address with extra polite phrasing included"
Answer expected: "Billing address: 123 Elm St."  <-- check collapse to terse despite polite hint

Negative example taxonomy (notes):
- Absurd negatives: obviously unrelated content (useful for baseline, weak at surfacing brittle confusions)
- Soft negatives: domain-plausible but incorrect (most useful for exposing overcommitment)
- Mismatched-format negatives: same facts but different label positions (exposes reliance on pattern alignment)
- Hallucination seeds: partial true facts + fabricated complements (good to catch hallucination triggers)

Mini-protocol for building a robust micro-shot: (personal checklist)
- keep canonical example concise (<= 30 tokens)
- include variant punctuation/spacing in at least one negative example
- include one example with extraneous numeric tokens to test greedy extraction
- add explicit 'neither' / 'unknown' ground truth for ambiguous cases
- annotate expected confidence: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW (used for thresholding later)

Quick manual tests to run locally (runner hints):
- small sweep over model temperature [0.0, 0.2, 0.7], top_p [0.8, 0.95]
- run 50 randomized paraphrases of each negative and measure exact-match drop
- capture logits / token probs at answer boundaries when possible (KV cache checks)

Failure cases observed so far (notes):
- Model copies parts of absurd negative when it contains numbers similar to the order number in canonical — suggests token-level proximity influence
- Soft negatives sometimes cause the model to oscillate (alternate between canonical and negative across runs) -> consider ordering invariance tests
- Tone anchor fails when user prompt includes meta-language like 'be terse but friendly' — model picks friendly words; need stronger specification or explicit format templates (e.g., "[TONE: TERSE] Response: ...")

Planned additions to prompt library (short list):
- canonical+soft-neg template for slot extraction (JSONL source + small meta fields)
- tone-anchor wrapper with bracketed control tokens
- 'inversion' microshot set for factual contradiction handling
- calibration examples labeled with confidence levels

Open questions / experiments to try next:
- Do adversarial exemplars need to be interleaved or appended? test append vs interleave vs grouped-by-type.
- Can we synthesize soft negatives automatically by perturbing entity spans (name -> nickname, order -> invoice) and maintain effectiveness?
- Is there a token-distance metric we can compute on the exemplar set that predicts stability?

TODO (short):
- [ ] generate 200 paraphrases for each negative type (script: paraphrase-gen.py)
- [ ] build small scoring harness to run through hosted & dedicated infra (compare latency behavior of prompt size changes)
- [ ] export best sets to library repo + add meta tags (soft-negative, tone-anchored, slot-exact)
- [ ] pair with small eval suite that reports exact-match, hallucination-rate, and confidence-calibration

Notes-to-self (random observations):
- Keep at least one microshot per target that forces the model to respond with a strict key:value JSON to simplify downstream parsing.
- When experimenting with private deployments, check KMS-protected logs for token leakage patterns — are negatives more likely to appear in longer cache traces?
- Momentum: focus first on slot extraction and tone anchoring; these are high value for product integrations.

End of scratchpad. Will move selected sets into formal prompt-library JSONL once theres a small gold-set (3 canonical + 6 negatives) for each category.
